sections.title: Executive investment summary: a real niche franchise priced as if the plan has already been delivered

blocks.text: [F] Yash Highvoltage designs, manufactures and tests condenser-graded transformer bushings: the insulated gateways through which high-voltage or high-current power enters and leaves a transformer (AR2026 p.47). [F] The range covers oil-impregnated-paper (OIP) condenser bushings from 15 kV to 245 kV, resin-impregnated paper/synthetic (RIP/RIS) bushings from 24 kV to 245 kV, high-current bushings of 24-52 kV and 4,000-25,000 A, wall-through and oil-to-oil bushings, plus retrofit, on-site testing and repair services (PPT May 2026). [F] All manufacturing is in one plant at Khakharia, Savli taluka, near Halol, Vadodara. A greenfield RIP/RIS plant at Jarod, Vadodara is being commissioned (AR2026 p.11).

[F] It makes money by selling engineered-to-order bushings, mostly to transformer OEMs, at a point in time. All FY26 revenue was recognised at a point in time, none over time (AR2026 p.185). [F] Today's RIP product, about 83% of FY26 revenue, is assembled and tested in India around a capacitive core that is imported, historically from Switzerland (PPT May 2026; CALL Jun 2025). [MC] Management says this import dependence is why RIP bushings are currently sold only in India (CALL Jan 2025; PPT May 2026).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation already requires the impossible. [F] At Rs 1,244, the shares trade at 100.5x trailing earnings, 65.9x EV/EBITDA and 19.3x book (NUMBERS). [E] The reverse DCF implies about 87% a year sales growth for five years, against a 10% base case and 16.5% starting growth in the bull case (NUMBERS).

2. Profits are not turning into cash. [F] FY26 cash from operations was Rs 8.8 cr against PAT of Rs 37.3 cr (AR2026 p.168). CFO/PAT fell from 0.48 to 0.24 (NUMBERS). [F] Inventories more than doubled, from Rs 29.7 cr to Rs 66.6 cr, while revenue grew 57% (AR2026 p.166).

3. The headline margin is flattered. [F] The presentation shows FY26 EBITDA of Rs 60.4 cr (25.7%) labelled 'excluding Other Income'. Its own gross-profit line is computed on total income, which includes Rs 5.8 cr of other income (PPT May 2026). [E] Statutory EBITDA excluding other income is about Rs 56.7 cr (24.1%). Our statements data shows Rs 57 cr (24%) (NUMBERS).

4. The 'near debt-free' description has lapsed. [E] Borrowings of Rs 31.1 cr plus leases of Rs 6.5 cr exceed cash of Rs 20.1 cr: about Rs 17.5 cr of net debt at March 2026, against a net cash position of about Rs 47 cr a year earlier (AR2026 p.166). [MC] Management still calls the balance sheet 'near debt-free' (CALL May 2026).

5. Execution slippage and cost creep on the key project. [MC] The greenfield was guided at Rs 90 cr and 'fully operational' by mid-2026 (CALL Jun 2025), then 'INR100 crores plus' (CALL Oct 2025). [F] It is now Rs 153 cr, with commissioning in H2 FY27 (AR2026 p.9). [MC] Commercial production is targeted for October 2026 (CALL May 2026).

6. Technology is licensed, not owned. [F] RIP bushings rely on imported cores. [MC] Core-making know-how comes from a Swiss consultant, and the core-supply agreement with the former shareholder MGC Moser Glaser runs to mid-2027 (CALL Jan 2025; CALL May 2026). [MC] Type-test outcomes for in-house cores are unproven (CALL May 2026).

7. Governance is light for the valuation. [F] The board has five members, two of them independent. The promoter's spouse sits on the audit committee and receives consultancy fees and lease rent (AR2026 p.72, p.89). [F] An independent director, Suril Mehta, works at K C Mehta & Co LLP (AR2026 p.37), which is the company's internal auditor (AR2026 p.74). [F] The MD's pay rose 107% to Rs 2.89 cr, 53x the median employee (AR2026 p.87).

8. Dilution and promoter sell-down. [F] A preferential issue at Rs 721 of up to 12,62,131 shares and 8,32,177 warrants (about Rs 151 cr) was approved on 22 June 2026 (AR2026 p.69). [F] 4,04,000 ESOPs carry a Rs 5 exercise price (AR2026 p.206). [F] Promoter holding fell from 57.94% (Mar-26) to 53.79% (Sep-26) (NUMBERS).

9. Customer concentration rising at the top. [F] One customer bought Rs 44.2 cr in FY26, against Rs 15.9 cr for the largest customer in FY25 (AR2026 p.209). [E] That customer's share rose from 10.6% to 18.8%, and the customer is not named.

10. Control and process lapses. [F] A Rs 2.10 cr cyber fraud: payments were diverted through impersonation of a China-based supplier (AR2026 p.208). [F] The stock reported to the bank at March 2026 was Rs 11.8 cr (17.8%) below book stock (AR2026 p.202).

subsections.title: Key debates: where the market may be wrong, both ways

items: Is the order book revenue? [AI] Bulls treat the Rs 400 cr+ order book as near-certain revenue. [MC] Management describes 'blanket orders for the next 24 to 36 months' (CALL May 2026). [AI] Such orders may be call-off frameworks rather than firm schedules. The AR does not define how the order book is measured or its cancellation terms.

Is FY27 guidance internally consistent? [MC] Management guided 40-45% growth and, in the same call, an invoicing target of Rs 360-400 cr (CALL May 2026). [E] 40-45% growth on Rs 235 cr gives about Rs 329-341 cr, which does not reach Rs 360 cr. The two figures are not reconciled.

Margins: structural or shortage rent? [MC] Management attributes the gain to scale, price recovery in a shortage and hedging (CALL May 2026). [AI] Two of those three drivers are cyclical. Bears may underrate the fact that the RIP core localisation benefit has not yet started.

Sukrut: growth engine or footnote? [F] Sukrut is a 50% joint venture with Quality Power, equity-accounted from 8 January 2026 (AR2026 p.194, p.71). [AI] Its revenue will never appear in Yash's consolidated revenue line, only 50% of its profit. Bulls citing a Rs 150-160 cr revenue target [MC] (CALL May 2026) may be double counting.

Is the stock simply too expensive for any outcome? [AI] The counter-argument is that our DCF's 10% base growth is mechanically derived from a short history and is below the actual 57% growth. Even so, the bull case at 16.5% starting growth yields Rs 160.8 per share against Rs 1,244 (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [AI] The market treats Yash as a scarce, approval-protected beneficiary of the transformer super-cycle, and the operating evidence supports that: volumes +26%, order book 2.7x in a year, exports doubling. Our variant view is that the 2027-28 story depends on three unproven events: in-house RIP cores passing type tests, a new plant ramping, and export approvals for an Indian RIP make. Meanwhile, the reported financials already show cash strain: CFO/PAT 0.24, inventory up 125%, and a swing to net debt. A headline margin that includes other income, plus a promoter group that is diluting and selling, should temper any premium for 'quality'. Even taking management's 40%+ CAGR at face value, it is less than half the growth our reverse DCF says the price requires (NUMBERS).

sections.title: Business model: an assembly-and-test model moving upstream into core manufacture

items: 1. Enquiry and design: [F] 3D CAD and FEM simulation are used for each rating, with customisation for voltage, current and utility specification (AR2026 p.26).
2. Approval: [F] customers, utilities and consultants approve a make. [F] The company has 125+ type-tested products (AR2026 p.27; PPT May 2026).

3. Core: [F] for OIP, condenser cores are wound in-house on high-speed winding machines, dried and oil-impregnated in SCADA-controlled autoclaves (AR2026 p.26). [F] For RIP/RIS, the capacitive core is currently imported (PPT May 2026).
4. Assembly: [F] flanges, insulators (porcelain or silicone), terminals and oil systems are assembled, with oil flooding for OIP (PPT May 2026).
5. Testing: [F] in-house NABL-accredited labs run high-voltage tests up to 600 kV, impulse tests to 1,500 kVp, partial discharge, tan delta, capacitance and DFR (AR2026 p.27).
6. Dispatch and after-sales: [F] export-grade packing; retrofit, on-site testing and repair services (AR2026 p.27; PPT May 2026).

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and why

blocks.text: [MC] In January 2025 the CFO gave material-to-sales ratios of about 60% for RIP, 70-75% for OIP and 30-35% for high current, and product EBITDA of 20-22%, 13-15% and 45% respectively (CALL Jan 2025). [E] The actual group materials-to-revenue ratio was 54.7% in FY25 and 53.3% in FY26 (AR2026 p.167). That is lower than the 60-62% blended figure the CFO quoted, and the two are not reconciled. [AI] On these figures, value capture today comes from approvals, design and testing rather than core manufacture. High-current and export OIP lines appear to earn the highest margins, and RIP earns volume. Making the core in-house would move the largest bought-in cost, which management says is 'maybe a bit more' than 35-40% of material cost [MC] (CALL Jun 2025), into the company's own value added.

[F] Fixed-asset turnover was 4.5x in FY26 and capex was about 25% of sales in both FY25 and FY26 (NUMBERS). [F] Job-work charges were only Rs 1.19 cr (AR2026 p.187). [AI] So far this has been a moderately asset-light assembly model. Jarod (Rs 153 cr, about 65% of FY26 revenue [E]), the planned 550 kV and brownfield capex, and the preferential raise move it towards a capital-heavier, vertically integrated model.

blocks.text: [F] Our DCF model projects five years of free cash flow to the firm: EBITDA less tax on EBIT, less capex, less the change in net working capital. Growth fades linearly from a starting rate to a year-5 rate, with a Gordon terminal value; equity value is EV less borrowings (NUMBERS). [F] Base inputs: TTM sales Rs 235 cr; EBITDA margin 23%; starting growth 10%, the median of 3-year, 5-year and TTM growth capped at 0-30%; D&A 2.6% of sales; capex equal to depreciation plus new sales divided by fixed-asset turnover of 4.04x; working capital 56.5 days; tax 25.2%; WACC 15% (cost of equity 15%: risk-free rate 7%, equity risk premium 7%, beta 1.15); terminal growth 5.5%; 2.988 cr shares (NUMBERS).

[AI] Drivers: sales growth is held at 10% because the growth rule can only use the short history available. EBITDA margin is held at 23%, slightly below FY26's 24%. FCFF turns positive at once because the rule ties capex to incremental sales at historical asset turnover. That conflicts with the reality of a Rs 153 cr plant, Rs 35 cr of capital commitments and a Rs 66.6 cr inventory build. [AI] The base case is therefore conservative on growth and generous on cash conversion. The two errors offset partly, not fully.

sections.title: Final thesis: a good small business carrying a great-company price

blocks.text: [AI] Yash is one of very few approved independent bushing makers in a market where transformer demand exceeds bushing supply. Its FY26 results were strong on every operating line: revenue +57%, units +26%, order book Rs 400 cr+, exports more than doubled, about 24% statutory margin [F] (AR2026 p.65-68). If the Jarod plant produces type-tested in-house cores in FY27, the company moves up the value chain, removes its largest imported cost and gains the right to export RIP. That combination could support several years of high growth and higher margins [MC] (CALL May 2026).

[AI] The price already discounts more than double management's own growth guidance for five straight years (NUMBERS). The FY26 earnings came with almost no operating cash, a doubling of inventory and a swing to net debt. The headline margin is flattered by other income. The technology underpinning 83% of revenue is still imported from a former partner whose supply contract ends in 2027. The plant that is meant to fix this is late and over its original budget. And governance (related-party payments, internal-auditor conflict, rising MD pay, promoter sell-down, deep-discount equity issuance) is weaker than the multiple implies.
